# The same split named twice, once hyphenated and once not.
#
# A guid is written either way and both resolve to the same split — GnuCash's
# own windows show the hyphenated form, so a reader copying from one and from
# an export gets one of each. Everything that compares guids here normalises
# first; the duplicate guard compared the raw strings, so this passed it.
#
# What it produces past the guard is what the guard exists to stop: the split
# is claimed twice, so `amount:` is *required* to state 80.00 for the 40.00
# that moved; the attach is idempotent, so the lot ends with one split; and the
# block then scores two slots against that one, so the invoice is judged
# changed on every import of an unedited file — unposted, its posting
# destroyed, rebuilt, for ever.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming the repeated guid, with nothing
# attached.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-02-27
    amount: 80
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    Transaction "5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445"
      PaymentSplit "8192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445566778"
      PaymentSplit "8192A3B4-C5D6-E7F8-0912-233445566778"
